title: Run a whole program
starter:
type arg = Lit of int | Name of string

let apply (op : string) (a : int) (b : int) : int =
  match op with
  | "add" -> a + b
  | "mul" -> a * b
  | "max" -> max a b
  | _ -> failwith op

let run (prog : (string * string * arg * arg) list) : int =
  let env = Hashtbl.create 16 in
  let value = function Lit n -> n | Name s -> Hashtbl.find env s in
  let last = ref 0 in
  List.iter (fun (name, op, x, y) ->
    let a = value x in
    let b = 0 in
    let v = ignore (op, a, y); 0 in
    Hashtbl.replace env name v;
    last := v) prog;
  !last
hints: `value` turns a `Lit` into its number and looks a `Name` up in `env`.
The last blank is `apply op a b`. `Hashtbl.replace` then saves it so later lines can use it.

answer.code:
type arg = Lit of int | Name of string

let apply (op : string) (a : int) (b : int) : int =
  match op with
  | "add" -> a + b
  | "mul" -> a * b
  | "max" -> max a b
  | _ -> failwith op

let run (prog : (string * string * arg * arg) list) : int =
  let env = Hashtbl.create 16 in
  let value = function Lit n -> n | Name s -> Hashtbl.find env s in
  let last = ref 0 in
  List.iter (fun (name, op, x, y) ->
    let a = value x in
    let b = value y in
    let v = apply op a b in
    Hashtbl.replace env name v;
    last := v) prog;
  !last
answer.explain: For each line, `run` turns both operands into numbers (looking names up in `env`), calls `apply`, and saves the answer under the line's name. Later lines find it there. That loop is a complete interpreter for this tiny language.
